PROJECT 01  /  SOVEREIGN AGENTIC AI WORKBENCH

1. Introduction

A user investigating equipment failure may need to connect a manual, an inventory record and an incident log.
Document search identifies candidate files, while a language model can synthesize a response. However, an
institution also needs to know whether the user is allowed to access those documents, whether the answer is
supported and whether a requested action requires authorization. These concerns belong to different parts of the
system and need different tests.

The Sovereign Agentic AI Workbench addresses this workflow through local document ingestion, scoped retrieval and
constrained orchestration. “Sovereign” denotes the intended ability to host the model endpoint within an
institution-controlled environment. The present implementation checks configured endpoint locality and runs in a local
container deployment; it does not establish an air-gapped or legally certified environment.

The motivating domain in the evaluated prototype is synthetic pump maintenance. Part identifiers, event dates and
failure causes provide inspectable facts. We do not claim that this corpus represents the complexity of a real industrial
knowledge base. Its role is to support functional and exploratory tests, including missing evidence and adversarial
instructions embedded in a source.

This is an unpublished manuscript draft based on inspected implementation and retained experiments. It makes no

Abstract

Institutional document assistants must connect natural-language answers to accessible evidence while controlling
actions that affect organizational workflows. We describe a local AI workbench integrating workspace-scoped
document retrieval, a deterministic evidence threshold, persisted task execution and owner approval for a report tool.
The implementation uses a Go API, Python AI service, PostgreSQL/pgvector, object storage and a locally configured
model endpoint. Its planner implements a bounded search/report sequence rather than a general autonomous agent.
